summary: Milestone M2 (Access, work pools and Case visibility) verified across its five documented steps. 48 of 48 cross-artefact references resolve (1 unclassifiable criteria value), no artefact's recorded deploy position contradicts its type, and the merged manifest built with no member collision and no API-version conflict (7 types, 19 members, 62.0). Two of three executable milestone acceptance tests pass; M2-T1 (check_access_model.py --manifest-dir artefacts) exits 1 against a declared exit 0 on a single 244-character description WARN in M2-S01, a step built five days before the rule existed and never rebuilt by the F-15 fix. Verdict not-ready on that failing test alone. M1's F-01 is CLOSED by M2-S03's Profile layoutAssignments, proven with a negative control; F-12 is CLOSED at the tooling. Six manual lines go to the human, one of which (Tier 2's queue mailbox) does not hold against its artefact and must not be ticked as written.
confidence_rationale: Step 10 rubric: one unclassifiable reference (the sharing rule's bare RecordTypeId criteria value) caps the score at MEDIUM. Nothing pulls it to LOW - every step was documented, no declared checker was missing, no artefact directory was empty, the earlier-milestone inventory built, and every declared acceptance test ran.

findings.title: M2 acceptance test M2-T1 exits 1 on a 244-character description WARN; the plan declares exit 0
findings.detail: check_access_model.py --manifest-dir artefacts returns exit 1 with one WARN: PSVP-DESC-02, artefacts/M2-S01/permissionsets/Case_Intake_Integration.permissionset-meta.xml description is 244 characters (> the 200-character headroom, < the 255-character platform limit). The checker's main() ends 'return 1 if normalized else 0' (line 177), so every severity including WARN exits non-zero. M2-S01 was built and tested 2026-09-06 and recorded exit 0; the DESC rules landed 2026-09-11 in commit 4da8e6c92 to close F-15, which rebuilt M2-S02 and M2-S03 under 200 characters and did not rebuild M2-S01. The test's declared assertion (no dangerous system permission, no migratable permission on a profile) holds. Deploy-time consequence: none - mock deploy run 3 validated this exact file among 32 components with 0 errors.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild M2-S01 (documented -> running, reason F-16) trimming the description under 200 characters - and the 250-character CustomPermission description with it - then re-test, re-document and re-run /verify-milestone. Alternatively the planner restates M2.acceptance_tests[0].expected at v6. Blocking for the verdict, not for the gate.

findings.title: The three DESC-rule checkers disagree on whether a WARN exits non-zero
findings.detail: Three checkers read the same 244-character description in this run. check_access_model.py (PSVP-DESC-02) exits 1; check_permission_set_architecture.py (PSA-DESC-02) exits 0; check_permission_set_group_composition.py (PSGC-DESC-02) exits 0. Whether a description-length advisory can fail a milestone therefore depends on which checker the plan happened to declare, not on anything about the artefact. The three rules were added in one change to close one finding; their exit policies were not aligned in that change, and F-16 is the first time it has mattered.
findings.recommendation: Align the exit policy across the three skills in one change, deciding once whether a length WARN is exit-worthy. Two of the three already exit 0.

findings.title: reports/MILESTONE-M1-package.xml is stale and still carries the bare CompactLayout member a deploy already rejected
findings.detail: The committed merged M1 manifest declares member 'Case_Intake' under CompactLayout - the exact form mock deploy #3 rejected with "An object 'Case_Intake' of type CompactLayout was named in package.xml, but was not found in zipped directory". artefacts/M1-S01/package.xml was rebuilt to the object-qualified 'Case.Case_Intake' (rebuild #3, mtime 2026-09-11 20:12); the merged manifest was last written 2026-09-09 16:16 and never regenerated. Mock deploy #4 does not discharge it: mock_deploy.py:resolve_manifest_text() reads reports/MILESTONE-<id>-package.xml only when exactly one --milestone is named with no --step mixed in, and run #4 passed --step M1-S01 --step M1-S02, so the manifest it validated was merged on the fly from the step files. F-13 is closed in the step manifest and open in the committed merged one. MILESTONE-M2-package.xml carries no CompactLayout member and is unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate MILESTONE-M1-package.xml on M1's next verification run; until then a human merging M1+M2 by hand must take Case.Case_Intake. Not fixed here - one milestone per invocation, and M1's manifest belongs to M1's verification run.

findings.title: check_record_type_layouts.py resolves the layout half of a Profile reference and not the record-type half
findings.detail: Negative control: a Profile whose recordTypeVisibilities names Case.Ghost - a record type that exists nowhere in the tree - still exits 0 with 0 findings, identically with and without --strict. A dangling layoutAssignments/layout, by contrast, fires a LOW naming the ghost layout and exits 1 under --strict. All 9 recordTypeVisibilities references in this build resolve, proven independently in the reference table rather than by this exit code - so nothing is wrong in the artefacts. What is wrong is the claim the exit code carries: steps[M2-S03].acceptance_tests[1].description says the run resolves 'any Profile-sourced record-type reference (12)', traceability.md REQ-026 repeats it, and decisions.md D-M2S03-07 sources F-01's closure to the same run. The layout half of that claim is earned; the record-type half is not asserted.

findings.title: Recorded deploy positions put the sharing rule (7) ahead of the group it shares to (9)
findings.detail: SharingRules:Case at position 7 references Support_Tier_2, a Group the workbook files at position 9 (routing). Read as a staged sequence that dependency runs backwards, and a sharedTo naming an absent group is a deploy failure (M2-S05/deploy-order.md marks the exact platform behaviour UNVERIFIED and ships the group in the same package rather than testing the assumption). Mitigated three ways: the step graph is right (M2-S05 depends_on [M1-S01, M2-S04]); the step's own deploy-order.md names the dependency and says 'Deploy M1-S01 and M2-S04 first, or include them in the same request'; and mock deploy run 3 sent all seven steps as one request and validated 32 of 32. The contradiction is in the ten-position bookkeeping, not in the build - and it is live for anyone staging a deploy by position.
findings.recommendation: At v6, record the groups at the access layer alongside the permission sets they are peer to, or annotate position 9 with 'groups must precede position 7's sharing rule'.

All five M2 deploy-order.md files get it right: M2-S01 emits deploy start --dry-run for the sandbox plus a separate deploy validate --target-org <your-production-alias> --test-level RunLocalTests for production, and the other four emit deploy start --dry-run only. metadata-builder applies the correct form to new work; F-08's residue is confined to two files that predate it.

process_observations.observation: The F-15 remediation loop closed end to end and the org caught what three green checkers did not: mock deploy runs 1 to 3 went 10 errors on 30 components, to 0 on 30, to 0 on 32.

M2-S03 did the job M1's report assigned it: F-01 had been open for two milestones because layoutAssignments lives on a Profile root no step had produced, and three profiles closed it with a negative control proving the checker reads them.

Every M2 deploy-order.md names its own ungrounded elements rather than smoothing them over - M2-S05 Decision 1 argues against the manifest form the step itself wrote and states what to do if a deploy rejects it.
Three of the six manual lines arrived with file-checkable evidence already gathered by the step tester, which narrows what a human at the gate must judge to the part that genuinely needs judgment.

A skill version bump moved a finished step from green to red with no signal: M2-S01 was documented and passing on 2026-09-06, and a rule added on 2026-09-11 to fix a different step's failure made it fail, with nothing in the loop re-running its tests.
Three checkers read the same 244-character description and returned three different exit policies, so whether a WARN can fail a milestone is currently an accident of which checker the plan cited.

The same omission recorded three times is still one line in plan.json: assumptions[A1].steps[] names M2-S05 alone while four steps carry artefacts A1 shaped, and W03, O-M2S02-03 and O-M2S03-03 are three agents finding it on three different steps.

Every other derived view in this build is regenerated from plan.json, but the merged milestone manifest is written once per verification run - so MILESTONE-M1-package.xml went stale the moment M1-S01 was rebuilt and the tool that would have caught it took a different code path.
Whether a 200-character headroom WARN should be able to fail a milestone acceptance test has two defensible answers, and the plan currently gives both depending on which checker a test declares.

Case_Tier1 and Case_Tier2 are byte-identical apart from label and description, and the two Tier profiles likewise - whether they should collapse depends on whether the two teams are expected to diverge on access later, which no clarification answers.

This line certifies the configuration; proving the denial against a live user is M5's UserRecordAccess test.
